questions.q: What actually makes an AWS subnet "public"?
options: A --type public flag set when the subnet is created
It's the first subnet created in the VPC
Its route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 traffic to an Internet Gateway
Every subnet in a VPC is public by default
questions.explain: AWS has no literal public/private flag on a subnet — the distinction lives entirely in whether its route table points internet traffic at an Internet Gateway.

options: A feature only available in a default VPC
An EC2 instance you size and patch like a server
A horizontally scaled, AWS-managed VPC component that enables internet connectivity and performs NAT for instances with public IPs
A per-subnet firewall that filters traffic by port
questions.explain: An IGW is a managed component with no capacity to plan — it's the target a route table points at, and it performs the NAT between private and public IPs.

questions.q: A subnet's route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to an Internet Gateway, but an instance inside it has no public IP. Can the internet reach that instance directly?
options: Only if the instance is in the default VPC
Yes, the route alone makes it reachable
No — a route to the IGW alone isn't enough; the instance also needs a public IP address
Only if the subnet is in a different Availability Zone
questions.explain: A public route and a public IP are two separate requirements — missing either one means nothing on the internet has a way to reach the instance.

options: It can only exist in the default VPC
It has a route to the Internet Gateway but a smaller CIDR block
It is always the last subnet created
Its route table has no route to an Internet Gateway
questions.explain: A private subnet simply lacks a route to an IGW, so nothing inside it is directly reachable from the internet.

options: Attaching an Internet Gateway to a VPC
Creating a route table entry pointing to the IGW
Converting a private subnet into a VPC
Telling a subnet to automatically assign every new instance a public IP at launch
questions.explain: It's a subnet attribute that automates giving new instances a public IP, instead of requesting one by hand every time.
